research_topic: Can we predict the next pandemic?
scope: Zoonotic spillover, outbreak early warning, pandemic escalation, and preparedness decision support.
allowed_conclusions: Stage-specific risk can be estimated, ranked, calibrated, and linked to preparedness decisions.
Exact prediction of the next pathogen, place, and date is not established by the evidence base.
Surveillance, verification, and response capacity remain necessary even when predictive models improve.
prohibited_conclusions: A proposed model has predicted the next pandemic.
Any ecological or social correlate proves a causal future-outbreak mechanism.
An unvalidated score justifies autonomous public-health action.

evidence_cards.claim: Host and viral traits can inform spillover prioritization.
Emerging zoonotic disease patterns are associated with global ecological and reporting context; event-data limitations matter.
Reservoir ecology and human exposure should be modelled as separate evidence layers.
Spillover and onward spread are related but distinct infection-dynamic processes.
Early-warning effectiveness depends on the surveillance-system context and data collection strategy.
Event-based reports can complement formal global surveillance after validation.
Wastewater surveillance offers a complementary community signal with interpretation challenges.
Zoonotic-virus machine-learning evaluation can conceal lineage and sampling failures.
Overstated prediction should not displace surveillance investment.
